indications: Used for pain relief and fever reduction in adults and children over 12 years.
dosage: Take 2 tablets (500mg) every 4-6 hours, not exceeding 8 tablets in 24 hours. Do not exceed 3000mg per day. For chronic use, consult a physician.
warnings: Do not exceed the recommended dose. May cause liver damage if taken in large quantities. May cause stomach upset. Avoid alcohol while taking. Pregnancy and lactation may pose risks. Consult a doctor for usage in children under 12. Some patients may experience allergic reactions, causing rash, breathing difficulties.
contraindications: Not safe in patients with compromised liver function. Overdose may cause severe liver damage.
interactions: Alcohol consumption while taking Paracetamol may increase risk of liver damage.

indications: Used for relief of mild to moderate pain including headache, dental pain, menstrual pain, and musculoskeletal pain.
dosage: Adults: Take 1-2 tablets (200-400mg) every 4-6 hours as needed. Maximum daily dose: 1200mg (6 tablets). Take with food or milk to reduce stomach irritation.
warnings: May cause stomach bleeding, especially in elderly patients. Do not use if you have a history of stomach ulcers. May increase risk of heart attack or stroke with prolonged use. Avoid during third trimester of pregnancy. May interact with blood thinners.
contraindications: Not recommended for patients with active peptic ulcer, severe heart failure, or severe kidney/liver impairment. Do not use in third trimester of pregnancy.
interactions: May interact with aspirin, blood thinners (warfarin), SSRIs, ACE inhibitors, and diuretics. Concurrent use with alcohol may increase risk of stomach bleeding.
